body:
> Could you also describe your use case and how you plan to use the command completion feature?
Have you installed Cubic via Cargo, Snap, or Homebrew?

I used Cargo for installing `cubic` because I really do not like Snap and I don't normally use Homebrew unless I'm using an immutable system. Anyone that installs `cubic` the same way, or by curling a release binary wouldn't be able to have the completions auto-generated upon installation (unless completions are contributed to each upstream shell and packaging format; I'd love to be wrong about this) and would be unlikely to discover them if the `completions` command is hidden.

Typically, if a tool doesn't already have completions for my shell (Fish), then I'll probe `--help` for some way to generate them. If one exists, then I'll do something like:

```sh
# if I suspect the tool completions will change often:
echo 'cubic completions fish | source' > ~/.config/fish/completions/cubic.fish

# or if the tool is unlikely to add new subcommands/args:
cubic completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/cubic.fish
```

With all that said, I _could_ hide the arg if it's a requirement for acceptance of the PR, but I am the type of user that avoids CLIs without completions and I think that doing so would make them much harder to discover.

+.. _recover disk:
+
+Recover Data from a VM Disk Image
+==================================
+
+This guide shows how to retrieve files from a Cubic virtual machine that can
+no longer boot or is otherwise inaccessible via ``cubic ssh``. The VM disk is
+a standard ``qcow2`` image, so ``qemu-img`` and ``qemu-nbd`` can read it
+directly from the host.
+
+Stop the Virtual Machine
+------------------------
+
+The disk image must not be in use by a running VM before it is mounted on the
+host:
+
+.. code-block::
+
+    $ cubic stop <instance>
+
+Locate the Disk Image
+---------------------
+
+Cubic stores each instance under the user data directory:
+
+* Linux: ``$XDG_DATA_HOME/cubic/machines/<instance>/machine.img``
+  (typically ``~/.local/share/cubic/machines/<instance>/machine.img``)
body:
The Snap installation path is missing. The code checks `SNAP_USER_COMMON` before `XDG_DATA_HOME` on Linux, so Snap users have a different data directory.
Suggest adding:

>  * Snap: ``$SNAP_USER_COMMON/cubic/machines/<instance>/machine.img``
>     (typically ``~/snap/cubic/common/cubic/machines/<instance>/machine.img``)

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+base_sha="${1:-${BASE_SHA:-}}"
+head_sha="${2:-${HEAD_SHA:-HEAD}}"
+
+if [[ -z "$base_sha" ]]; then
+    echo "::error::Base commit SHA is required."
+    exit 2
+fi
+
+for revision in "$base_sha" "$head_sha"; do
+    if ! git cat-file -e "${revision}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
+        echo "::error::Commit '${revision}' is not available in the checkout."
+        exit 2
+    fi
+done
+
+if [[ -z "$(git log "${base_sha}..${head_sha}" --pretty=tformat:"%H")" ]]; then
+    echo "No pull request commits to validate."
+    exit 0
+fi
+
+commit_subject='^(feat|fix|refactor|docs|chore|revert): .+'
+
+git log "${base_sha}..${head_sha}" --pretty=tformat:"%H" | while read -r commit_hash; do
+    short_sha="$(git rev-parse --short "$commit_hash")"
+    message="$(git show -s --format=%B "$commit_hash" | tr -d '\r')"
+    subject="$(printf '%s\n' "$message" | sed -n '1p')"
+    last_line="$(printf '%s\n' "$message" | sed '/^[[:space:]]*$/d' | tail -n 1)"
+
+    body_lines="$(
+        printf '%s\n' "$message" |
+            awk '
+                NR == 1 { next }
+                /^[[:space:]]*$/ { next }
+                /^Signed-off-by:/ { next }
+                { body++ }
+                END { print body + 0 }
+            '
+    )"
body:
The `awk` block is doing a lot of work for a simple intent. Since a well-formed commit message always has the structure:

> subject
> blank line
> body
> Signed-off-by: ...

 That's a minimum of 4 lines. You can replace the entire `awk` command with a line count:
` line_count="$(wc -l <<< "$message")"`
 and then check `[[ "$line_count" -lt 4 ]]` in the condition below.
This is simpler and requires no `awk` dependency.
